A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 21 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison. Reorganized appendix material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-agent simulation results for disaster response, misinformation containment and public-goods provision, including baseline comparisons, ablations and model-specific results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations and adds disaster-response results for additional models and a mixed-model team in Section 5.3 and Table 3.

M1.justification: Agents still exchange messages and independently choose actions under implicit consensus; explicit consensus still imposes a collective action. Role prompting and adaptation without fine-tuning remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions and mixed-model evaluations do not establish a new coordination procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three simulated tasks: disaster response, misinformation containment and dynamic public-goods provision. Added model configurations operate within the existing disaster-response task.

E2.justification: The evaluated coordination comparators remain explicit consensus, Single LLM, No Interaction, Random Strategy and No Diversity, as confirmed by Figures 3–4 and Table 2. Additional LLM backbones do not introduce new comparison procedures.

E3.justification: v2 adds targeted N=30 evaluations with Deepseek-V3, o3-mini and a mixed-model team. Section 3.2 revises the discrete-action reference from an arithmetic expectation to the mode and specifies task-specific distances. Section 4.2 describes coverage as cells attended, although Appendix C.1 retains containment within two rounds. These are reported setting and metric changes; recomputation of retained results is not established.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 examines sensitivity to stronger models, a reasoning model and heterogeneous model composition. It tests whether the implicit-consensus advantage persists across these configurations. Existing role and interaction ablations, volatility analyses, toy-model analysis and detailed dialogue examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs per setting and five random seeds or initializations in the experimental appendix. Averaging and the existing shaded plots are retained; no new confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 Table 3 adds explicit/implicit coverage rates of 0.81/0.98 for Deepseek-V3, 0.70/0.95 for o3-mini and 0.75/0.96 for the mixed team. Original Tables 1–2 and v1 Tables 3–5, now v2 Tables 4–6, retain their numerical results. Figure 5 changes proportions without changing plotted values.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 revises mathematical definitions: discrete actions use a modal reference, and deviation receives Manhattan, Jaccard or normalized absolute-distance definitions. The random-iteration model is retained from v1 Appendix C in v2 Appendix E; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstracts and contribution statements retain the same central claims: an implicit-consensus framework and diversity measures, with moderate disagreement improving adaptation in three dynamic scenarios. Additional model experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of o3-mini's limited implicit-consensus advantage, including possible overthinking, and of stronger-model influence in mixed-team voting. Limitations replace specific model exclusions with broader computational and scalability constraints. The main text also presents the toy model more cautiously as context for structured diversity.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added comparison's N=30 setting and exact mixed-team composition of 15 GPT-4o and 15 GPT-4o-mini agents, alongside more explicit distance calculations. Existing prompt templates, temperature 0.7, max_token 256, implementation description and code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Du et al. on multi-agent debate, Cho et al.'s RoundTable and Cuadron et al. on overthinking, while removing Nomura et al. The revised discussion more explicitly contrasts dynamic adaptation with factual consensus and static-task decision-making; the broader positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, methodology, experimental setup, results discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Baseline descriptions are consolidated, method explanations are expanded, and appendices are reorganized to foreground cross-scenario results and dialogue interpretation.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, changes Figure 5's aspect ratio, updates Figure 2's caption and rearranges several displays. Figure 6 moves into Appendix E, and the retained cross-scenario tables move to Appendix A. Existing figure artwork and table designs are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The additional model and mixed-team evaluations partly address v1's acknowledged model-coverage limitation, while rewritten method descriptions clarify consensus mechanisms and shared action spaces. These provide a modest gain in support and readability. The gain is limited by unresolved reporting issues, particularly the differing coverage definitions in v2 Section 4.2 and Appendix C.1, and unchanged uncertainty reporting.
